preamble: Word-initial change of the palatal glide [j] to the glottal fricative [h], a debuccalization with devoicing. In Greek one set of Proto-Indo-European initial *y- became h- (Proto-Hellenic *yêkʷər > ἧπαρ hêpar 'liver'; *Hyós > ὅς hós 'who'), while another set became z- (ζυγόν 'yoke'). In Armenian, word-initial յ y came to be pronounced [h], so Classical Յովհաննէս Yovhannēs (< Greek Iōánnēs) is Modern Հովհաննես Hovhannes.

examples.note: Initial h- is shown in 5th-century BCE Attic; later lost (Modern ήπαρ ípar).

examples.from: Old Armenian Յովհաննէս Yovhannēs (< Greek Ἰωάννης Iōánnēs)
examples.note: In Classical orthography յ is [j] but [h] word-initially; modern spelling writes the [h] with հ.
